title: Generate Parentheses
keyIdea: Backtracking that only makes valid moves: add '(' while open < n, add ')' only while close < open. Every string that reaches length 2n is valid, so nothing needs checking at the end.

approaches.name: Generate every string, then check
approaches.idea: Build all 2^(2n) strings of ( and ), keep the balanced ones.
approaches.why: Most of the strings are invalid and get thrown away.

approaches.name: Backtracking with open / close counts
approaches.idea: backtrack(open, close, curr): length 2n → save; open < n → add (; close < open → add ).
approaches.why: Only valid prefixes are ever built: one path per answer (the Catalan number).

options: Only when close < open, so it closes an earlier '('

quiz.q: Why is no validity check needed at the end?
options: Every move keeps the prefix valid, so a full-length string is always balanced

quiz.q: How many valid strings are there for n = 3?
Why doesn't this code need to undo (pop) after the recursive call?
options: curr + '(' makes a new string for the call; the caller's curr never changes
